intent: Test ubuntu_perf_fixes.sh to 100% line coverage and take it off the shell coverage allowlist, leaving one untested lib in fixes/lib.
changes: Added SYSCTL_DROPIN_DIR, SYSTEMD_UNIT_DIR (twice) and EARLYOOM_CONF_FILE seams, each defaulting to the real path so production behaviour is unchanged
Deliberately left the add_undo lines with their literal /etc paths: the undo script runs on the real system, not in the sandbox, so seaming them would have written a broken undo
Extended the existing ubuntu_perf_harness.sh with the three new overrides, three more default stubs (nvidia-smi, nvidia-persistenced, dpkg) and the _t_unit / _t_sysctl_file readers
Added 59 assertions over 14 cases across two files covering all four functions
Removed ubuntu_perf_fixes.sh from meta/shell-coverage-allowlist.txt, taking it from 86 to 85 entries

verification.evidence: ubuntu_perf_fixes.sh: 81/81 lines = 100.00%, exit 0, no case timeout.

verification.command: shell_coverage_jail.sh --timeout 600s --measure bt_audio.sh --min 100 (canary, with the two new test files present)
verification.evidence: bt_audio.sh: 127/127 lines = 100.00%. This is the lib a previous test file silently broke, so it is re-measured after every addition to this suite.

verification.command: bash meta/scripts/check_shell_coverage.sh .../ubuntu_perf_fixes.sh, AFTER deleting its allowlist line
verification.evidence: 'every checked shell library meets the coverage bar', EXIT 0.
Both 'No such file or directory' after the suite ran, confirming the seams kept every write inside the throwaway tmpdir.
All fixes lib test files passed; 31 + 28 = 59 new assertions, 0 failed.

verification.command: shellcheck + shfmt on the lib, the harness and both test files
verification.evidence: No findings, zero suppressions. Lib is 219 lines, under the 250-line cap.

risks: fix_earlyoom writes a config on a machine that may already have one; the test asserts the .bak backup is taken before the overwrite, which is the behaviour that makes that safe.
The undo lines are asserted to contain the REAL /etc paths, so a future seam applied to them would fail these tests rather than silently producing an undo script that removes nothing.

fix_failed_sssd's detection loop breaks at the first failed unit while its masking loop re-checks each one; case 7 covers the single-failure arm specifically, since a naive implementation would mask all five.
rollback: git revert the commit, then re-add the ubuntu_perf_fixes.sh line to meta/shell-coverage-allowlist.txt
Re-run check_shell_coverage.sh to confirm the gate passes again with the exemption restored
